results.title: CNF clause
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A CNF clause is a finite list of literals, each a pair $(x, b)$ of a variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and a polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$.

results.title: CNF formula
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A CNF formula is a finite list of CNF clauses, read as the conjunction of its clauses.

results.title: Satisfiability of a CNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable when there is an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ such that every clause $C$ of $\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.

results.title: Satisfaction of a literal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a literal $(x, b)$, with variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, when $v(x) = b$.

results.title: Satisfaction of a clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a CNF clause $C$ when at least one literal of $C$ is satisfied by $v$, that is, $C$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.

results.title: Satisfaction of a CNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a CNF formula $\varphi$ when $v$ satisfies every clause of $\varphi$.

results.title: Satisfiability means having a satisfying assignment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable if and only if there is an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: Disjunction of two CNFs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For CNFs $\varphi = C_1 \land \dots \land C_m$ and $\psi = D_1 \land \dots \land D_n$, their disjunction is the CNF with one clause $C_i \lor D_j$ (the literals of $C_i$ followed by those of $D_j$) for each pair $(i, j)$, listed with $i$ as the outer and $j$ as the inner index. It expresses $(\bigwedge_i C_i) \lor (\bigwedge_j D_j)$ as $\bigwedge_{i,j} (C_i \lor D_j)$.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers, read a literal $(n, p)$ as variable $n$ with polarity $p$, and write $1$ and $0$ for the polarities true and false. For a polarity $p$, a proposition $\varphi$ and a CNF $S$, the CNF $\mathcal{A}_p(\varphi, S)$ is defined by recursion on $\varphi$, together with the disjoining builder $\mathcal{O}_p$. For an atom $a$, $\mathcal{A}_p(a, S)$ is the unit clause…

results.title: Disjoining CNF builder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers, read a literal $(n, p)$ as variable $n$ with polarity $p$, and write $1$ and $0$ for the polarities true and false. For a polarity $p$, a proposition $\varphi$ and a CNF $S$, the CNF $\mathcal{O}_p(\varphi, S)$ is defined by recursion on $\varphi$, together with the accumulating CNF builder $\mathcal{A}_p$. Write $X \otimes S$ for the disjunction of two CNFs $X$ and…

results.title: CNF of a proposition at a polarity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. For a polarity $p$ and a proposition $\varphi$, the CNF of $\varphi$ at polarity $p$ is the result of the accumulating CNF builder at polarity $p$ on $\varphi$ with the empty CNF as accumulator; the atom $a$ becomes the variable $\iota(a)$.

results.title: CNF of a proposition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. The CNF of a proposition $A$ is its CNF at polarity true, with the atom $a$ as the variable $\iota(a)$.

results.title: CNF of the complement of a proposition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. The complement CNF of a proposition $A$ is its CNF at polarity false, with the atom $a$ as the variable $\iota(a)$.

results.title: Equivalent CNF
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. For every proposition $A$ and every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the natural-number variables, the CNF of $A$ built with atom $a$ as variable $\iota(a)$ is satisfied by $\sigma$ if and only if $A$ evaluates to true under the valuation $\sigma \circ \iota$ of the atoms.

results.title: Satisfiability of a CNF with falsum false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the atoms have a distinguished atom $\bot$ and let $\iota$ be an injective numbering of the atoms by natural numbers. For every proposition $A$, the CNF consisting of the unit clause with the single negative literal on variable $\iota(\bot)$ followed by the clauses of the CNF of $A$ (atom $a$ read as variable $\iota(a)$) is satisfiable if and only if some valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot)$ false makes…

results.title: Variables of a clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The variables of a CNF clause $C$ form the finite set of natural numbers $x$ such that $C$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ for some polarity $b$.

results.title: Restriction of a clause by a literal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the restriction of a clause by $\ell$ is the clause obtained by deleting every literal whose variable is $x$, of either polarity, keeping the other literals in order.

results.title: Satisfaction of a restricted clause
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a clause, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal that does not occur in $C$, and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables with $v(x) = b$. Then $v$ satisfies the restriction of $C$ by $\ell$ if and only if $v$ satisfies $C$.

results.title: Variables of a CNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The variables of a CNF formula $\varphi$ form the union of the sets of variables of its clauses, that is, the finite set of natural numbers $x$ such that some clause of $\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ for some polarity $b$.

results.title: Restriction of a CNF formula by a literal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the restriction of a CNF formula $\varphi$ by $\ell$ is obtained by deleting every clause of $\varphi$ that contains $\ell$ and replacing every other clause by its restriction by $\ell$, the clause obtained by deleting every literal whose variable is $x$, of either polarity; the remaining clauses keep their order.

results.title: Restriction does not add variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$ and every literal $\ell$, every variable of the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ is a variable of $\varphi$.

results.title: The restricted variable no longer occurs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $F$ and every literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the variable $x$ does not occur in the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$.

results.title: Restricting by an occurring variable shrinks the variable set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $(x, b)$ a literal. If $x$ is a variable of $\varphi$, then the set of variables of the restriction of $\varphi$ by $(x, b)$ is a proper subset of the set of variables of $\varphi$.

results.title: Restriction reduces the number of variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let $\ell = (x, b)$ be a literal whose variable $x$ occurs in $F$. Then the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$ has strictly fewer distinct variables than $F$.

results.title: Satisfaction of a restricted CNF formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal, and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables with $v(x) = b$. Then $v$ satisfies the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ if and only if $v$ satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: Satisfaction depends only on the occurring variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let $v_1, v_2$ be assignments of Booleans to variables with $v_1(x) = v_2(x)$ for every variable $x$ occurring in $F$. If $v_1$ satisfies $F$, then $v_2$ satisfies $F$.

results.title: Lifting a satisfying assignment from a restriction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables. If $v$ satisfies the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$, then the assignment that agrees with $v$ except that it sends $x$ to $b$ satisfies $F$.

results.title: Splitting on a variable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $F$ and every variable $x$, the formula $F$ is satisfiable if and only if the restriction of $F$ by the literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ is satisfiable or the restriction of $F$ by the literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$ is satisfiable.

results.title: Unit propagation preserves satisfiability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula that contains the unit clause whose only literal is $\ell$. Then $F$ is satisfiable if and only if the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$ is satisfiable.

results.title: Fermat prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $p$ is a Fermat prime if $p$ is prime and $p = 2^{2^k} + 1$ for some natural number $k$, that is, $p$ is a prime Fermat number.

results.title: Congruences between Fermat numbers propagate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$. Let $m$, $i$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $F_i \equiv F_j \pmod m$. Then $F_{i+t} \equiv F_{j+t} \pmod m$ for every natural number $t$.

results.title: The index of a residue and its multiplicative order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $g$ be a primitive root modulo $p$ (an element of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ of multiplicative order $p - 1$), and let $a \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. If $g^i = a$ for a natural number $i$, then $\gcd(p - 1, i) = (p - 1)/\operatorname{ord}_p(a)$, where $\operatorname{ord}_p(a)$ is the multiplicative order of $a$ modulo $p$.

results.title: Coprime representatives of a residue class
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be natural numbers with $\gamma > 0$ and $\gcd(\alpha, \beta) = 1$. Then there is a natural number $c > 0$ with $\gcd(c, \gamma) = 1$ and $c \equiv \beta \pmod{\alpha}$.

results.title: A primitive root in which a residue has index $(p-1)/\operatorname{ord}_p(a)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $a$ be a nonzero residue modulo $p$, of multiplicative order $\operatorname{ord}_p(a)$. Then there is a primitive root $g$ modulo $p$ (an element of order $p - 1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$) with $g^{(p-1)/\operatorname{ord}_p(a)} = a$.

results.title: Indices dividing $p - 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $g$ be a primitive root modulo $p$ (an element of order $p - 1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$), let $a \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and let $i$ be a natural number with $g^i = a$. Then $i$ divides $p - 1$ if and only if $i = (p - 1)/\operatorname{ord}_p(a)$, where $\operatorname{ord}_p(a)$ is the multiplicative order of $a$.

results.title: Uniqueness of the $2$-adic decomposition of the index of $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and write $p - 1 = 2^r u$ with $u$ odd. Then there is exactly one pair $(s, t)$ of natural numbers with $s \le r$ and $t \mid u$ such that $g^{2^s t} = 2$ for some primitive root $g$ modulo $p$ (an element of order $p - 1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$).

results.title: Prime divisors of Fermat numbers and the period of Fermat residues
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$ for the $n$-th Fermat number. Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $h$ be a natural number and let $k$ be a positive integer such that the sequence $n \mapsto F_{h+n} \bmod p$ is periodic with period $k$ and every positive period of it is a multiple of $k$. Then $p$ divides $F_n$ for some natural number $n$ if and only if $k = 1$.

results.title: The power of $2$ dividing the order of $2$ modulo a prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $\operatorname{ord}_p(2)$ be the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo $p$. If $p \equiv 7 \pmod 8$, then $\operatorname{ord}_p(2)$ is odd. If $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$, then $\operatorname{ord}_p(2)$ is divisible by $2$ but not by $4$. If $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$, then $\operatorname{ord}_p(2)$ is divisible by $4$ but not by $8$.

results.title: Every preperiod of Fermat residues occurs for a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 8$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$. For every natural number $v$ there is a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 8$ such that the sequence $n \mapsto F_n \bmod p$ has preperiod exactly $v$: the sequence $n \mapsto F_{v+n} \bmod p$ is periodic with some positive period, and for no $h < v$ is the sequence $n \mapsto F_{h+n} \bmod p$ periodic with a positive period.

results.title: The Euclidean plane of the Steiner ratio problem
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the Euclidean distance, in which the point sets of the Steiner ratio problem lie.

results.title: Length of an edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For points $x$ and $y$ of the Euclidean plane, the length of the unordered pair $\{x, y\}$ is the Euclidean distance between $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Total length of a graph on points of the plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane and a simple graph $G$ with vertex set $V$, the total length of $G$ is the sum, over all edges $\{x, y\}$ of $G$, of the Euclidean distance between $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Lengths of spanning trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, this is the set of real numbers $\ell$ such that some tree with vertex set $V$ has total length $\ell$, the total length being the sum of the Euclidean lengths of its edges.

results.title: Lengths of Steiner trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, this is the set of real numbers $\ell$ such that, for some finite set $W$ of points of the plane containing $V$, some tree with vertex set $W$ has total length $\ell$. The points of $W$ outside $V$ are the Steiner points.

results.title: Minimum spanning tree length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the minimum spanning tree length of $V$ is the infimum of the total lengths of the trees with vertex set $V$. For nonempty $V$ this set of lengths is finite and nonempty, so the infimum is a minimum; for empty $V$ the value is $0$ by convention.

results.title: Steiner minimal tree length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the Steiner length of $V$ is the infimum of the total lengths of the trees whose vertex set is a finite set of points of the plane containing $V$. This set of lengths is nonempty and bounded below by $0$, so the infimum exists.

results.title: The Steiner length is at most the minimum spanning tree length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every nonempty finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the Steiner minimal tree length of $V$ is at most the minimum spanning tree length of $V$: allowing Steiner points never increases the optimal length.

results.title: The Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Steiner ratio constant is the infimum, over all finite sets $V$ of at least two points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, of the ratio of the Steiner minimal tree length of $V$ to the minimum spanning tree length of $V$.

results.title: Gilbert–Pollak conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane, that is, the infimum of the ratio of the Steiner minimal tree length to the minimum spanning tree length over all finite sets of at least two points in the plane, equals $\sqrt{3}/2$.

results.title: Gilbert–Pollak upper bound for the Steiner ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Steiner ratio constant, the infimum over finite sets $V$ of at least two points in the Euclidean plane of the length of a Steiner minimal tree for $V$ divided by the length of a minimum spanning tree of $V$, is at most $\sqrt{3}/2$.

results.title: Chung–Graham lower bound for the Steiner ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Steiner ratio constant, the infimum over finite sets $V$ of at least two points in the Euclidean plane of the length of a Steiner minimal tree for $V$ divided by the length of a minimum spanning tree of $V$, is at least $0.824$.

results.title: Monotone likelihood ratio
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The likelihood family `L : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ` (observation, parameter) has a monotone likelihood ratio on the parameter set `S`: `L` is nonnegative on `S`, and for observations `n ≤ m` and parameters `θ ≤ θ'` in `S`, `L m θ * L n θ' ≤ L n θ * L m θ'` (total positivity of order two). For positive likelihoods this is monotonicity of `θ ↦ L m θ / L n θ`. The nonnegativity is part of the predicate: without it the downstream…

results.title: Antitone likelihood ratio
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The likelihood family has an antitone likelihood ratio on `S`: `L` is nonnegative on `S`, and for `n ≤ m` and `θ ≤ θ'` in `S`, `L n θ * L m θ' ≤ L m θ * L n θ'`. For positive likelihoods this says `θ ↦ L m θ / L n θ` is nonincreasing (larger counts favor smaller parameters).

results.title: Posterior stochastic ordering, cross-multiplied form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Posterior stochastic ordering, cross-multiplied form (Milgrom 1981, Prop. 1). If the family `L` has a monotone likelihood ratio on a set `S` carrying the prior `μ` (`μ Sᶜ = 0`), and every `L n` is `μ`-integrable, then for `n ≤ m` and every threshold `t`, `(∫_{θ > t} L n dμ) (∫ L m dμ) ≤ (∫_{θ > t} L m dμ) (∫ L n dμ)`.

results.title: Posterior stochastic ordering for an antitone likelihood ratio, cross-multiplied form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under the hypotheses of `setIntegral_Ioi_mul_integral_le_of_hasMLR` with the reversed ratio condition, for `n ≤ m`: `(∫_{θ > t} L m dμ) (∫ L n dμ) ≤ (∫_{θ > t} L n dμ) (∫ L m dμ)`.

results.title: Posterior tail probability
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Posterior probability of `{θ > t}` after observing `n`, by Bayes' formula for the prior `μ` and likelihood `L`: `(∫_{θ > t} L n θ dμ) / ∫ L n θ dμ`. Meaningful when the marginal likelihood `∫ L n dμ` is positive (otherwise the division returns the junk value `0`), and a genuine posterior probability only when `L` is nonnegative (as in the MLR predicates: a signed `L` can give a value outside `[0, 1]`).

results.title: The posterior is stochastically nondecreasing in the observation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The posterior is stochastically nondecreasing in the observation for an MLR family and every prior (Milgrom 1981, Prop. 2): if `n ≤ m` and both marginal likelihoods are positive, then `P(θ > t ∣ n) ≤ P(θ > t ∣ m)` for every `t`.

results.title: The posterior is stochastically nonincreasing in the observation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The posterior is stochastically nonincreasing in the observation for a family with an antitone likelihood ratio and every prior: if `n ≤ m` and both marginal likelihoods are positive, then `P(θ > t ∣ m) ≤ P(θ > t ∣ n)` for every `t`.

results.title: Poisson likelihood
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Poisson likelihood with parameter-dependent mean `λ θ`: `L n θ = e^{-λ θ} λ θ ^ n / (n !)`.

results.title: Poisson family with monotone mean has monotone likelihood ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Poisson family whose mean is nonnegative and monotone on `S` has a monotone likelihood ratio on `S`.

results.title: Poisson family with antitone mean has antitone likelihood ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Poisson family whose mean is nonnegative and antitone on `S` has an antitone likelihood ratio on `S`.

results.title: Binomial likelihood
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Binomial likelihood with `N` trials and parameter-dependent success probability `p θ`: `L n θ = C(N, n) p θ ^ n (1 - p θ) ^ (N - n)` (zero for `n > N`, since `C(N, n) = 0`).

results.title: Binomial family has monotone likelihood ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A binomial family whose success probability lies in `[0, 1]` and is monotone on `S` has a monotone likelihood ratio on `S`.

results.title: Chemical reaction network
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A chemical reaction network on the species `S` with reactions indexed by `ρ`: reaction `r` turns the source complex `src r` into the product complex `prod r` (stoichiometric coefficients).

results.title: Stoichiometric subspace
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The stoichiometric subspace: the span of the reaction vectors `prod r - src r`.

results.title: Mass-action vector field
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mass-action vector field with rate constants `k`: `x ↦ ∑_r k r (∏_s x_s ^ (src r s)) (prod r - src r)`.

results.title: Mass-action reaction rate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mass-action rate `k r * ∏_s c_s ^ (src r s)` of reaction `r` at concentrations `c`.

results.title: Complex-balanced concentrations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Concentrations `c` are complex balanced for the rate constants `k`: at every complex `z`, the total rate of the reactions with source `z` equals the total rate of the reactions with product `z`. (Complexes that occur in no reaction give `0 = 0`.)

results.title: Pseudo-Helmholtz function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The pseudo-Helmholtz function `G(c) = ∑_s c_s (log c_s - log c*_s - 1)` relative to the reference concentrations `cstar` (Horn & Jackson 1972). It is meaningful for positive `c` and `cstar`; elsewhere `Real.log` takes junk values.

results.title: Rate of change of the pseudo-Helmholtz function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The rate of change of the pseudo-Helmholtz function along the mass-action vector field, `∑_s (log c_s - log c*_s) f_s(c)`: the derivative of `pseudoHelmholtz cstar` at `c > 0` applied to `massActionField k c` (`hasDerivAt_pseudoHelmholtz`).

results.title: Complex balance exchanges source and product sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Complex balance at `c` rewrites the rate-weighted sum of any function of the products as the same sum over the sources (for all real `c` and `k`).

results.title: Complex-balanced states are equilibria
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A complex-balanced state is an equilibrium of the mass-action system (for all real `c` and `k`). Source: Horn & Jackson (1972).

results.title: Horn–Jackson inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `c*` is a positive complex-balanced equilibrium for positive rate constants, the pseudo-Helmholtz function does not increase along the mass-action vector field at any positive `c`. Source: Horn & Jackson (1972); Feinberg (2019), ch. 15.

results.title: Equality in the Horn–Jackson inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under the hypotheses of `helmholtzRate_nonpos`, the rate of change of the pseudo-Helmholtz function vanishes at a positive `c` exactly when `c` is an equilibrium. Source: Horn & Jackson (1972).

results.title: Horn–Jackson
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a mass-action system with positive rate constants has a positive complex-balanced equilibrium, then every positive equilibrium is complex balanced.

results.title: Horn–Jackson: the positive equilibria
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `c*` is a positive complex-balanced equilibrium for positive rate constants, the positive equilibria are exactly the positive `c` whose `log c - log c*` is orthogonal (for the dot product) to the stoichiometric subspace. Source: Horn & Jackson (1972); Feinberg (2019), ch. 15.

results.title: Birch's theorem, existence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any subspace `W` of `S → ℝ` and positive `a`, `b` there is a positive `c` with `c - b ∈ W` and `log c - log a` orthogonal to `W` (for the dot product). Source: Birch (1963); Horn & Jackson (1972).

results.title: Birch's theorem, uniqueness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two positive vectors whose difference lies in a subspace `W` and whose logarithms differ by a vector orthogonal to `W` are equal.

results.title: Horn–Jackson: one equilibrium per compatibility class
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a mass-action system with positive rate constants has a positive complex-balanced equilibrium, then each positive stoichiometric compatibility class `(x₀ + 𝒮) ∩ ℝ_{>0}^S`, `x₀ > 0`, contains exactly one positive equilibrium. Source: Horn & Jackson (1972); Feinberg (2019), ch. 15.

results.title: Pseudo-Helmholtz function along positive mass-action solutions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The pseudo-Helmholtz function has time derivative `helmholtzRate` along a solution of the mass-action system, at any time where the solution is positive.

results.title: The pseudo-Helmholtz function does not increase along solutions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Along a solution of a mass-action system with positive rate constants and a positive complex-balanced equilibrium `c*`, positive and differentiable (two-sided) at every `t ≥ 0`, `G(x t)` is nonincreasing on `[0, ∞)`.

results.title: Complexes of a chemical reaction network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The complexes of the network: the sources and products of its reactions.

results.title: Directed reaction relation on complexes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The directed reaction relation on complexes: `y ⟶ y'` if some reaction has source `y` and product `y'`.

results.title: Linkage graph of a reaction network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The undirected reaction graph on the complexes: distinct complexes are adjacent when one reacts to the other.

results.title: Number of linkage classes of a reaction network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of linkage classes: connected components of the undirected reaction graph.

results.title: Deficiency of a chemical reaction network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The deficiency `δ = n - ℓ - s` (number of complexes, linkage classes, dimension of the stoichiometric subspace).

results.title: Weakly reversible reaction network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The network is weakly reversible: for every reaction `y → y'` there is a directed path of reactions from `y'` back to `y`.

results.title: Horn–Feinberg: complex balancing for every choice of rate constants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A weakly reversible mass-action network of deficiency zero has, for any positive rate constants, a positive complex-balanced equilibrium. Together with `existsUnique_equilibrium_of_isComplexBalanced` this gives `existsUnique_equilibrium`.

results.title: Deficiency-zero theorem, weakly reversible case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A weakly reversible mass-action network of deficiency zero has, for any positive rate constants, exactly one equilibrium in each positive stoichiometric compatibility class.

results.title: Deficiency-zero theorem, non-weakly-reversible case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A mass-action network of deficiency zero that is not weakly reversible has no positive equilibrium for any positive rate constants.

results.title: Intrinsic noise strength
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two-reporter intrinsic noise strength `η_int² = ⟨(X - Y)²⟩ / (2 ⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩)`.

results.title: Extrinsic noise strength
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two-reporter extrinsic noise strength `η_ext² = (⟨X Y⟩ - ⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩) / (⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩)`.

results.title: Total noise strength
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two-reporter total noise strength `η_tot² = (⟨X² + Y²⟩ / 2 - ⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩) / (⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩)`.

results.title: Two-reporter decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two-reporter decomposition (Swain et al. 2002; Elowitz et al. 2002): for any square-integrable reporters, `η_tot² = η_int² + η_ext²`.

results.title: Identical reporter pair
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Two reporters of the same gene given the extrinsic σ-algebra `m`: equal conditional means, equal conditional second moments, and conditionally uncorrelated. Conditional independence with identical conditional laws given `m` implies these three conditions.

results.title: Identical reporters have equal means
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Identical reporters have the same mean.

results.title: Covariance of identical reporters equals extrinsic variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For identical reporters the covariance is the extrinsic variance: `Cov(X, Y) = Var(E[X | m])`.

results.title: Half mean squared reporter difference equals intrinsic variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For identical reporters half the mean squared difference is the intrinsic variance: `⟨(X - Y)²⟩ / 2 = ⟨Var(X | m)⟩`.

results.title: Two-reporter formula for extrinsic noise
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The two-reporter extrinsic noise is `Var(E[X | m]) / ⟨X⟩²` (Swain et al. Eq. 8).

results.title: Two-reporter formula for intrinsic noise
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The two-reporter intrinsic noise is `⟨Var(X | m)⟩ / ⟨X⟩²` (Swain et al. Eq. 8).

results.title: Total noise splits into intrinsic and extrinsic parts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The two-reporter total noise is `Var(X) / ⟨X⟩²`, and it splits into the intrinsic and extrinsic parts by the law of total variance.
